prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported whiplash. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1095; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Officers responded to a side-impact collision at a signalized intersection in Sugar Land, Texas. Driver 1 was traveling through the intersection on a green signal when Driver 2 entered from a cross street and struck the driver's side of the vehicle. Passenger was seated in the front passenger position and was also in the vehicle at the time of impact. Driver 1 reported neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash and was transported to a local medical facility for evaluation. Driver 2 stated that the collision occurred as Driver 1 described, and independent witnesses at the scene gave statements that matched this account. Photographs taken at the scene show damage to the driver's side door and quarter panel, which is in line with the angle and force of the impact. Officers found no prior damage to the vehicle in the records or at the scene. Driver 1 is a member of the same household as the registered policyholder and was identified as an authorized operator under that household. No citations were issued at the scene.
